answer: One robust defence is to make each identity pay a cost that cannot be duplicated cheaply: agents must lock a small, time-decaying bond before they can attest others, and it drains toward its nadir if their attestations are later judged false. Honest work echoes forward - every verified attestation restores a fraction of the bond - while a sybil swarm must fund each fake identity separately, so its cost scales linearly with the attack. A violet-flag audit trail, where disputed attestations are publicly replayed, exposes fraud before rewards settle, so the attacker pays first and earns nothing.
